speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; have you noticed if the vomit is truly green or if there is blood in it? Additionally, has the baby passed any stool since birth, and was it green or black?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. The clinical picture of a term newborn with bilious vomiting, feeding intolerance, and a significant family history of pyloric stenosis (suggesting a potential chromosomal anomaly like Trisomy 21) strongly points to a proximal intestinal obstruction. The absence of stool since birth further supports this.
